dicas.texto: Você está indo bem! Para localizar um valor maior que 1 na reta, ajuda saber quantas unidades inteiras ele contém. Como você pode separar 33/12 em inteiros e uma fração menor que 1?

Clique no botão 'Convert'. Isso abrirá campos para a parte inteira e a fração. O enunciado já deu uma pista: ele menciona '2 e 9/12'. Tente colocar o 2 no campo da parte inteira e o 9/12 nos campos da fração.
O campo 'm1' é para o número inteiro (2). Os campos 'm2' e 'm3' são para a fração (9 e 12). Preencha-os e veja se o sistema aceita.
Após clicar em 'Convert', digite '2' no campo 'm1', '9' no campo 'm2' e '12' no campo 'm3'. Isso representa exatamente o número misto que você precisa para marcar na reta.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta "What is the fraction in the problem?" com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); reta numérica de 0 a 3 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 12 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, converter, marcar o ponto, concluir).

dicas.texto: In a fraction, the numerator tells how many parts or items are being counted.
Look at the number above the fraction bar in the fraction that describes the pen collection.
Use the total number of colorful pens as the numerator.
Type the total number of pens into the upper fraction box, field f1.
The denominator tells how many items make one whole group.
Find how many pens are in one dozen before entering the denominator.
One dozen is the unit used to measure Katie's collection.
Type the number of pens in one dozen into the lower fraction box, field f2.
A fraction is greater than one when it contains more than one complete whole.
Compare the numerator with the denominator to decide whether the fraction is greater than one.
There are enough groups of 12 in 33 to make more than one whole dozen.
After confirming that the fraction is greater than one, click the ... button to open the mixed-number fields.
A mixed number shows the complete wholes first and the remaining fractional part second.
Divide the numerator by the denominator to find the whole-number part and the remainder.
Use the number of complete groups of 12 for m1, the leftover pens for m2, and keep the group size as m3.
Fill m1 with the whole-dozen count, m2 with the remainder, and m3 with the denominator from the original fraction.
The whole-number part tells you which large interval contains the point.
Start at the whole-number location, then move forward by the fraction of the next interval.
From the mark for 2, count nine equal twelfth-intervals toward 3.
Place the point at the ninth small mark after 2, which is three quarters of the way from 2 to 3.
A correct point must represent both the whole dozens and the remaining fraction.
Check that the point lies between 2 and 3 and matches the fractional distance from 2.
Verify that the point is nine twelfth-intervals after 2, not at the beginning of the number line.
Once the point matches the converted mixed number and its decimal position, click ....

exercicio.statement:
Katie has a huge collection of colorful pens; she has 33 of them! If she were to describe the pen collection in number of dozens, it would be 33/12, or 2 and 9/12 dozens. Show the number of dozens of pens on the number line.
What is the fraction in the problem?

Start at the whole-number location, then move forward by the fraction of the next interval.
From the mark for 2, count nine equal twelfth-intervals toward 3.
Place the point at the ninth small mark after 2, which is three quarters of the way from 2 to 3.

misconceptions.description: O aluno foca apenas na parte fracionária do número misto.
misconceptions.feedback: You marked only the fractional part, but the collection includes 2 complete dozens. The point must be beyond 2 on the number line.

misconceptions.description: O aluno conta a marca do número inteiro como o primeiro intervalo.
misconceptions.feedback: You counted one interval too many. Count the intervals after the mark for 2; the ninth interval gives the correct location.

nodes.description: Confirm the point is at 2.75, then select Done.
nodes.instruction: Confirm the point is at 2.75, then select Done.

hints.message: A correct point must represent both the whole dozens and the remaining fraction.
Check that the point lies between 2 and 3 and matches the fractional distance from 2.
Verify that the point is nine twelfth-intervals after 2, not at the beginning of the number line.
Once the point matches the converted mixed number and its decimal position, click ....
